Sure, if you play AdVenture Capitalist you'll just watch yourself gather money forever. Why is that fun?

Because each tier takes ~10x as much money as the one before it, so as you progress further and further it takes longer and longer to get there.

Not every tier is the same - some are cheap, some you need to save up for, some have huge bonuses and some don't.

The reason why it's fun is because you optimize your investment strategy to reach the next tier as fast and effectively as you can. Which will pay off faster, dumping $100 in a hundred $1 investments that return at $0.01/hour or two $50 investments that return at $0.50 an hour? (Trick question - those are exactly equal. and then you realize that Earth on AdCap takes quadrillions of years to complete even if you spend enough money to bankrupt the entire world's economy and drop it after you clear Moon.(because Mars better be complete within like a week. Some cool ones, I guess:

Games like c(ode) (a while while back, there were people who made various plays on this game) were pretty neat but they didn't go that far. It's kinda like that old Upgrade Complete game in which you upgraded various convenience and mechanical features about the game but it's simply done in programming.

Digital Logic Design - Cross between a puzzle game and a clicker game, but with 100 times the clicks. It even has mild optimization elements. However, as it is based around programming (a subject I only like conceptually because actually programming is full of annoyances) I wasn't able to fully enjoy it. But it was a neat concept.

Bead Machine - Focused more on mechanical progress because the method for resource generation is by using parts inside a 2D grid (machine) to gain, transfer and turn resources into other resources, and was more puzzle than click. However, the resetting process is really annoying and it might take so long you'd want to quit playing. Instead of just resetting with a single click, you have to remove all your resources first, and this happens over and over. It felt artificial (and you also had a gain of 1 dollar point per second, so you'd have to click out at the exact time you had 0).
